title: Heat map
description:
A heat map colors a grid: `x_column` across, `y_column` down, `value_column` the color.
The default renderer packs two rows into one line (half blocks); `chart { renderer:
block }` gives every row a line and can write the values. See `:help dbdash-charts`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM d WHERE n < 5),
h(n) AS (SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 18)
SELECT 'Day ' || d.n AS day, printf('%02d', h.n) AS hour,
       abs((d.n * 7 + h.n * 13) % 50) AS requests
FROM d, h

show.description:

show.title: renderer: block, value { display: block }, format
show.description:
`chart { renderer: block }` gives every row its own line; `value { display: block }`
writes each value in its cell (black or white, whichever reads better), in the Python
`axes.y_axis.format`.

query.sql:

show.description:
Your own colors from low to high (`chart { color-scale }`, "#rrggbb" stops, ECharts
`inRange.color`) over a fixed range of the data (`scale_min` / `scale_max`): values
outside take the end colors.
